title: Equality of the fixed-scalar projection diamonds
statement:
theorem sixFunctorProjectionFinite_diamond_equality
    (S : SixFunctorDatum D C E n hn) (Q : SixFunctorCompactifiedSquare D)
    (K : sixFunctorFiniteCategory D C E n hn Q.X)
    (L : finiteTorConstructibleCategory C.l E n hn Q.Y.obj.left) :
    letI := Padic.finite_coefficientExtensionRing C.l E n hn
    let A := ULift.{u + 1} (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing C.l E n)
    let RX := CompactSupportFiniteProjection.realization
      (C := C) (E := E) (n := n) (hn := hn) Q.X
    let RY := CompactSupportFiniteProjection.realization
      (C := C) (E := E) (n := n) (hn := hn) Q.Y
    FiniteProjectionExchange.diamondLeft A Q.square Q.compactification
        (RX.inverse.obj K.obj) (RY.inverse.obj L.obj) =
      FiniteProjectionExchange.diamondRight A Q.square Q.compactification
        (RX.inverse.obj K.obj) (RY.inverse.obj L.obj)

source.place: Base-change paragraph, fixed-coordinate proper/open mate calculation

proof.text: Install the finite coefficient-ring instance for the positive level n. Apply the existing general fixed-scalar diamond_equality helper in FiniteProjectionExchangeTransposes to Q.square, Q.compactification, and the two inverse-realized inputs. This helper proves the same proper/open mate calculation for arbitrary finite coefficient rings and arbitrary derived objects: its two proper transposes coincide, injectivity of the adjunction gives the proper-route equality, and open_factor_assembly gives the diamond. The datum S is not needed for this fixed-coordinate identity.
